title: Somebody Said King Costs ₹450 Crore. Siddharth Anand Had One Word.
excerpt: Bollywood Hungama dropped the number. The director posted 'FALSE' on X. But with Suhana Khan's debut, Abhishek Bachchan as the villain, and 150 days of global shooting — whatever King actually costs, it's clearly everything Shah Rukh Khan has.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Shah Rukh Khan's *King* reportedly has a production budget over ₹450 crore.
  • Director Siddharth Anand labeled the ₹450 crore figure as 'FALSE', leaving the actual budget unclear.
  • The film features a star-studded cast, including Suhana Khan and Abhishek Bachchan.
  • Scheduled for release on December 24, 2026, *King* aims for a major holiday box office.
  • Bollywood's top films now routinely have production budgets between ₹300-400 crore.
The number landed like a grenade. https://youtube.com/watch?v=M3mfut2RdHk On Tuesday, **Bollywood Hungama** reported — exclusively, they stressed — that **Shah Rukh Khan**'s upcoming action thriller *King* has crossed ₹450 crore in production costs, making it the most expensive film of his career. Not including print and publicity. Not including his acting fees. Just the making of the thing. The claim spread faster than a *Pathaan* trailer. Industry watchers started doing the math. Social media lit up with comparisons to *Jawan* (₹400 crore) and *Pathaan* (₹350 crore). If the number was real, *King* would sit alongside the most expensive Indian films ever made — and SRK wasn't just competing with himself anymore. He was competing with the *Ramayana*. Then, on Wednesday morning, director **Siddharth Anand** posted a single word on X. > "FALSE." No elaboration. No context. No counter-number. Just one syllable, and the conversation shifted entirely. ![Suhana Khan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/4/45/The_Archies_film_poster.jpg) > **"Siddharth Anand said "FALSE" about the price tag."** Here's what makes this so delicious. Anand didn't say the film is cheap. He didn't deny that *King* is ambitious, or massive, or expensive. He denied the specific number — which means the real budget is still a mystery, and one that the industry is now even more obsessed with cracking. ## What We Actually Know About King Forget the budget for a moment. The facts alone make this the most anticipated Hindi film of the year. *King* has been shooting since May 2025. The team has logged over 150 days across multiple international locations, with some of the world's top stunt coordinators on set. That's fifteen months of production for a film that started as a focused action thriller and has reportedly evolved into something much bigger — a tentpole spectacle with global ambitions. **Siddharth Anand** is directing, fresh off the staggering commercial success of *Pathaan*, which turned into a cultural event in January 2023. This is his second collaboration with SRK, and the stakes could not be higher. The cast reads like a Diwali card from Bollywood royalty. **Suhana Khan** makes her theatrical debut opposite her father, reportedly playing his protégée in a story loosely inspired by Luc Besson's *Léon: The Professional*. **Abhishek Bachchan** plays the primary antagonist — a reunion of two of Bollywood's most iconic family names on opposite sides of the screen. **Abhay Verma** rounds out the core cast, while persistent industry buzz links **Deepika Padukone** to a powerful cameo and names like **Jaideep Ahlawat** and **Arshad Warsi** to supporting roles. On the music front, **Anirudh Ravichander** — the man who scored *Jawan* — is composing both the soundtrack and background score. If *Jawan*'s music was any indication, expect anthems designed to break streaming records before the film even opens.

The VFX is being handled in-house by **Red Chillies Entertainment**, SRK's own production company, which means the creative loop between star, director, and visual effects team is tighter than most studios can manage. ## The Christmas Date — and What It Means for Diaspora Audiences *King* is locked for **December 24, 2026**. That's a strategic 45-day gap after *Ramayana*'s expected Diwali release. Christmas is SRK territory — *Dilwale*, *Zero*, and *Dunki* all released in the festive window. For NRI audiences across the US, UK, and Canada, a Shah Rukh Khan Christmas release is practically a holiday tradition. Expect IMAX screenings, premium format rollouts, and the kind of global day-and-date release that *Pathaan* pioneered. The film will face a clash with major Hollywood tentpoles eyeing the same holiday corridor. The details are still shifting, but the trade is already treating *King* as the dominant domestic contender for Christmas 2026. ## The Real Story Behind the ₹450-Crore Drama The budget controversy — however briefly it burned — reveals something real about where Bollywood is right now. The top end of Indian cinema has entered a zone where ₹300-400 crore production budgets are routine for A-list tentpoles. *Ramayana*'s distribution rights alone reportedly fetched ₹350 crore. Ranveer Singh's *Pralay* is mounted at ₹300 crore. The numbers keep climbing.
Release Strategy for *King*
›Scheduled for December 24, 2026.
›Strategic release after *Ramayana*'s Diwali debut.
›Targets NRI audiences in US, UK, Canada.
›Expected to clash with major Hollywood releases.
Whether *King* costs ₹350 crore or ₹450 crore matters far less than what it represents: Shah Rukh Khan, three years away from a theatrical screen, betting everything on a single, definitive return. The kind of performance that either cements a legacy or redefines it. Siddharth Anand said "FALSE" about the price tag. Nobody's said "false" about the ambition.
